# Master Power Window Switch Repair

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove master power window switch, clean contacts with contact cleaner, then reinstall components. [t39]

[Partial] Remove door trim and switch, clean contacts with sandpaper and cleaner, then reassemble components. [t58]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove one end of the door trim piece by prying it up slightly.
2. Pull the master power window switch assembly out from under the trim.
3. Disconnect the electrical harness connector attached to the switch.
4. Use a Phillips screwdriver to remove and set aside three screws holding the switch to the trim.
5. Separate the white cover from the main switch body by prying one side loose with two small flat tools.
6. Rotate the loosened cover off completely while being careful not to crack the plastic or jab internal electronics.
7. Remove the power window lock button by pulling it straight up, but leave the door lock button in place if desired.
8. Spray electrical contact cleaner over the exposed green circuit board and gold contacts.
9. Pry open the white sub-covers on individual buttons to access their specific internal contacts.
10. Remove each metal wing rocker from its slot by pulling it out, noting which end is slightly larger.
11. Clean the blackened contact points on the main board using a fine grit sandpaper or wire brush.
12. Scrub the tips of the removed wing rockers with sandpaper until they are completely clean again.
13. [Partial] Slightly bend each cleaned wing rocker tip downward to ensure a tighter connection.
14. [Partial] Spray another light coat of contact cleaner over the reassembled components and let them dry.
15. Press the white sub-covers back onto their respective buttons one by one.
16. Snap the main white cover back into place around all the buttons.
17. [Partial] Reinstall the three Phillips screws to secure the switch assembly to the door trim.

_Procedure reported by [t58]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-repair-master-power-window-switch.8919/>_

## Tools

- Electrical Contact Cleaner [t39, t58]
- Sandpaper (one sheet) [t39]
- Two small flat-tip screwdrivers or eyeglass repair toolkit size tools [t39]
- One Phillips tip screwdriver or snow crab pick [t39]
- Sheet of sandpaper or wire brush (fine grit) [t58]
- Interior removal tool, plastic pry tool, or small flat-tip screwdrivers [t58]
- Phillips head screwdriver [t58]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Clean all buttons even if only one is malfunctioning to prevent future issues. [t39]
- [Partial] Work carefully as the assembly is mostly plastic and prone to cracking. [t39]
- Be careful with all components as the assembly is mostly plastic and prone to cracking. [t58]
- [Partial] Clean every button on the board even if only one window was acting up, or repeat this process sooner rather than later. [t58]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Removing the door lock switch unnecessarily, risking a ball bearing flying out of its spring housing. [t39]
- [Partial] Failing to align the wing rockers correctly due to their asymmetrical ends. [t39]
